symptom:
A TCP key-value server (server/main.go) stores each version of its data as a file gen.N in data/ and publishes it by replacing the symlink data/current with a link to the new generation. Recovery follows data/current. The filesystem is modelled strictly: a directory change survives a crash only if the directory was fsynced, and directory operations may persist out of order. The client remembers every PUT that was answered OK and reads them all back at the end. After publishing a generation the server deletes generations that are no longer needed.

Observed on seed 4: after repeated crashes the restarted server failed its startup check: the current symlink points at a generation that exists: current -> gen.57: open data/current: No such file or directory.

Expected: after any crash data/current must point at a complete, readable generation and all acknowledged puts must be present.
